title: Contract Pricing Agreement Claims Desk Note: Substitute Claim Amount
content:
# Substitute claim amount — claims desk calculation note (Contract Pricing Agreement)

**Shipment and invoice in view.** The claim the customer files, on the customer's most recent invoice on its Commercial Credit Account, for the latest regular shipment of the Corbett-approved substitute that filled the latest backorder on the customer's ship-tos (as the customer's Ship-To Fulfillment Account records show them), when that invoice is dated on the shipment's ship date or within 30 days after it and the shipment's ship date falls on or after the effective date of the substitute's protection line and fewer than the tier's discontinued item price protection days after it. Calendar days from one date to another count the later date and not the earlier one. Wherever a latest or most recent record of a kind is taken, it is the one with the latest date, and among records of the same date the one recorded first.

**Claim figures.**
- The claim's overbilling per unit is the billed unit price on the shipment less the protected price on the substitute's protection line, never below 0.
- The claim quantity is the quantity billed on the shipment.
- The claim amount is the overbilling per unit multiplied by the claim quantity; it is rounded half up to the cent once, on the final figure.
- A multiplier set for the claim multiplies the unrounded claim amount, and every credit set for it adds its percent of that same unrounded claim amount, before that rounding.

| Boundary (hypothetical protection period of 90 days) | In view |
|---|---|
| Invoice dated on the ship date | Yes |
| Invoice dated 30 days after the ship date | Yes |
| Invoice dated 31 days after the ship date | No |
| Ship date on the protection line's effective date | Yes |
| Ship date 89 days after that effective date | Yes |
| Ship date 90 days after it | No |

**Worked example (hypothetical).** Billed at 15.0000, protected price 12.5000, 40 units billed: overbilling 2.5000 per unit, claim amount 2.5000 multiplied by 40, which is 100.00.
